blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Noel Celis’s pulse still races whenever a motorcyclist pulls up alongside him at a red light, a legacy of countless nights photographing Philippine ex-president Rodrigo Duterte’s bloody drug war. “They call it riding in tandem,” the freelance photographer told AFP of the two-man teams that once roamed the capital, Manila, dealing out death, conceding it remained “scary” after years of death threats tied to his work. Duterte goes on trial at the International Criminal Court (ICC) on November 30 for the “crime against humanity of murder”, over killings that took place between 2011 and 2019.
